title: In-Memory SQL Query Object (Ad-Hoc Ast Composition)
pattern: Building a composite hierarchy of runtime objects (like `Criteria` and `QueryObject`) solely to construct query strings dynamically in memory.
why_bad: It bypasses compile-time query verification, hides the schema structure from compiler analysis, and introduces severe overhead due to runtime string formatting and memory allocation. It replicates an extremely weak, uncompiled version of a database query parser inside application memory.
detection: The presence of structs that contain raw strings for fields, operators, and parameters, combined with recursive traversal functions whose sole output is a database-bound query string.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If a query system is intended to receive dynamic, user-configured search preferences at runtime from a web UI to filter datasets, a structured Query Object is appropriate.
fix:
Utilize compile-time SQL macro providers or static query builders (such as Diesel or SQLx in Rust) where query semantics, parameters, and tables are validated during compilation.

```
// Compile-time checked static query utilizing a standard query framework
let active_users = users::table
    .filter(users::age.gt(21))
    .filter(users::name.like("John%"))
    .load::<User>(&mut connection)?;
```
source: [The Addison-Wesley signature series] Martin Fowler - _Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture_ (2015_2002, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Chapter 10 "Query Object"; Joshua Kerievsky - _Refactoring to Patterns_ (2004, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Chapter 7 "Replace Implicit Language with Interpreter".
